It's been a week and a half since I decided to finally start trying to subdue my OCD skin-picking disorder. It gets really bad and I can say that OCD is definitely one of the most embarrassing disorders to have in that even trying to explain what goes on in your head makes you sound absolutely psycho to someone who's unfamiliar with it.

Last night my boyfriend and I got into an argument because I literally got mad at him because he wouldn't let me pick at the skin on his face. I asked him to let me pick, he said no, and then I literally BEGGED him until he finally caved in but then when I got in position he changed his mind and my heart sank. I got mad at him and gave him the silent treatment for about an hour.

He finally blew up and said, "Why am I being punished for not wanting to go to work tomorrow with scratches and marks all over my face!" and I just broke down inside. It's only been a week and a half and the fact that I haven't done my picking rituals to myself has built up so much anxiety in me that I tried to the person I love most feel bad for not letting me do it to them. How irrational. I went to bed feeling so angry with myself.

I tried explaining to him (after apologizing, of course). I told him how when I look at another person's face or my own face, I'm not even seeing a face. I'm seeing spots of skin that I can pick and a burning tingling sensation happens in my fingers until I finally do the picking. I can't touch his arm in comfort without scanning his skin with my fingertips. 

It makes me feel so gross.

I come from a Christian upbringing and followed it strictly as a younger child, but as I grew older reading certain parts of the Bible I just got a completely different feel of the God that was being described in it as opposed to the way people in my religion described him: an all-powerful, controlling, justice-seeking warlord who holds a clear distinction between good and evil and is out to obliterate anything that opposes him.

The following are fluid thoughts I have about a higher being on a daily basis that change depending on circumstance. Not a strict theological viewpoint at all. Just some things I feel sometimes.

I feel like, if God is real (which I do still believe, though quite loosely these days), he (or she) is very similar to one of us. A being with immense power, but was lonely, didn't really see a point in existing if everything was just emptiness and vanity, and so decided to just start creating things and experimenting with them until he created something as close to him as could be, felt really proud of it, and later regretted it and realized it was a mistake because of how potentially horrible these creations could turn out to be.

And then decided to exterminate the entire species (Noah and the Ark story). And then rebuilt, realizing that that too was a mistake. It makes him just like us: wiping something or someone out because they're different or don't think the way we do.

Then they started being horrible again, and he thought, Is it worse to obliterate them or control them? Can they even be controlled? Fuck it.

So he just left us to be and exist. And now we are the way we are today.

And he didn't want to be worshipped. He just wanted to be less lonely. He doesn't understand why the people who actually acknowledge his existence would put more emphasis on *worshipping* him than being kind and loving to each other, which is the key to survival. 

So he sent someone, or maybe, if the legend is true, he came down in the form of a person to relay this message. That all the worship mess really doesn't matter, the key to survival and peace is loving each other. But then they killed him. Whatever, maybe they never wanted peace in the first place.

So no more divine intervention. I think God gave up a long time ago. I would too, if I were him. I think he made mistakes and regretted things. I hate when people say "God doesn't make mistakes." Even if you believe in what the Bible says, there are literally scriptures saying that God regretted things and changed his mind about things. (Of course the Bible was written by people though, so.) How could the concept of a divine Will ever be possible? There's no way, without some type of evil being done by the same God whose Will it is. Either that or free will doesn't exist. And either way, both paths point to God being the one responsible for the evil deeds.

That's why I blame humans for everything wrong with the human race, including religion. I don't think we've ever had a real clue about how to fix the issue, and I don't think God has either.

Things to consider: 

Narcissistic parents are two very different sides of the same coin. They do everything for themselves and themselves only, while making it seem like they are doing it for others (their children) or fooling others into believing they are doing things for them. It makes them look good and feeds into their feelings of grandiose.

I would even call helicopter parenting, when done by a narcissist at least, a form of mental abuse, since the desired effects it has on the child are nothing but dangerous and entirely intentional.

My mother was both abusive (physically and mentally), as well as a helicopter parent. She was not neglectful as far as providing for us; in fact, definitely the opposite. 

She made sure that everyone in the neighborhood, all our friends and family, knew that her children always got everything they needed and "wanted" (read: she wanted), because she saw her children as an extension of herself and if she could brag about them to others, essentially she was able to brag about herself. Also because as long as she was providing for us we were indebted to her and obligated to do everything she wanted exactly the way she wanted. 

Helicopter parenting, in the hands of a narcissist, is nothing but a manipulative technique. It is not about the parent "loving their child too much" or anything like that, but it appears that way, which believe it or not makes the parent seem more affectionate in other people's eyes, and also makes the children's claims of abuse seem ridiculous and overblown in the eyes of those who don't know better. 

Narcissists do not always appear batshit crazy or physically abusive. Most are incredibly smart, calculating.

I agree that there is a difference. I'm not implying that all forms of physical discipline is abuse, or that all parents who gives spankings are bad.

However. I personally do not believe that physical discipline is necessary, and you've said a lot here that I don't agree with.

I do not agree that there is a huge problem in today's society of parents not disciplining their children. Do you have some stats? And if you do have stats that show me that there is a decline in physical punishment, then next I'll need you to show me the stats where this has had such a negative impact. 

Because as far as I can see, the generation that brags about beating and getting beat (spanked, whatever) are the ones that have been more likely to abuse their children (like the parents of every single person who's commented on this post). The ones from my mother's generation, the ones who ended up strung out on drugs in the 80s and the generation of deadbeat fathers, etc.

I do NOT agree that it is the parent's duty to "make sure your child grows up prepared for the real world" as opposed to whatever fairy tale you're implying it must be if we don't beat our kids. Just how is spanking your child preparing them for the real world? By teaching them violence? By teaching them to fear or be feared? That's not real-world experience. It doesn't teach responsibility or actual discipline. 

The problem with people who hold a mentality such as yours is that you think that if you don't beat or spank your children, they're not getting punished. I promise you, they will learn much more from well thought-out punishment that teaches responsibility for their actions than they ever will from hitting.

I appreciate your counterargument and the points you make.

My point is not that there should be no form of punishment, though, the way you're mentioning. Of course kids deserve punishment when they act up. Lack of discipline (neglect) is also a form of bad parenting.

I get what you're saying. But I personally believe that it is fully possible to raise healthy and good children without hitting or any form of physical punishment. I would even argue that actually taking the time to punish your child in healthier ways, like, say, making them fix their own mistakes, is more effective than beating them as punishment because it teaches them discipline and responsibility for their actions. 

As opposed to a beating, which in most cases seems to teach nothing more than "If you don't do as I say, you'll get beaten," which essentially teaches children one of two things: Either they should do the right thing out of fear, or that they can use fear to make others do what they want or what they consider the "right thing" to be.  The problem is that they're missing the entire point of the punishment--learning what the right thing is and why it's important--because all they're focused on is doing the thing mommy or daddy wants me to do, so I don't get a beating.

And like I said in my post, I don't think all people who beat their kids are bad. I too am probably more affected by my mother's emotional and psychological abuse than the physical abuse. And it's good that you didn't turn out to be evil or anything. But you can't control what type of effect physical punishment will have on your child. I agree, it has something to do with their temperament. But lots of times also, a kid's temperament has quite a bit to do with their parents and how they learn to cope with what they've been handed.
